about: The mokata IDE's HTTP contract (0.0.26 P0, ID-API-CONTRACT). Every route the server answers is listed here (core) or in src/mokata/ide/features/<name>.contract.json (a feature); tests/test_p0_ide_api_contract.py boots the app on a fixture repo, sends every probe, and holds each answer to its entry. `version` changes only when an existing route changes shape incompatibly (the release bumps it, not a stage); adding a route does not bump it. Response schemas are a subset of JSON Schema (type, required, properties, items, enum, $ref to #/schemas) checked by mokata.ide.contract.validate; they pin each answer's keys and types, not its values. A governance route (runs, plan, lifecycle) on a repo mokata has not set up answers 200 with the NotInitialized state (0.0.26 P29); tests/test_p29_ide_uninitialized_repo.py holds every route to this contract on such a repo.
how_to_add_a_route: 1. ROUTE: add src/mokata/ide/features/<name>.py with `def routes(reg, ctx):` calling `reg.register(path, handler, kind=..., feature="<name>")` - do not edit server.py's list. Kinds: json (a sync read `handler(request) -> dict`, wrapped by the server's _json: 400 on ctx.bad_request, job=<kind> (+ job_label=) to run it as a job: the result, or 202 with the job's handle), read (async GET returning a Response), action (async POST), stream, page, static, hook. Every route is mounted behind the same guard (Host, pairing, Origin on POST). A path+method another feature owns is refused when the app is built.

2. CONTRACT: add src/mokata/ide/features/<name>.contract.json: {"routes": [{path, method, kind, params, responses: {"<status>": {media, schema}}, probes: [{query|body|path, status, demo?}]}]} - one probe per declared status; `demo: true` runs it on the SAMPLE server (use it for anything that would go online, start work, or needs SAMPLE data). Shared schemas live in this file's `schemas` (e.g. {"$ref": "#/schemas/Error"}).
3. TEST: the contract test needs no edit - it probes every entry. Add your own business test for what the route MEANS; the contract only pins its shape.
4. FRONTEND (optional): static/features/<name>.js (and .css) are loaded by the page automatically; call window.mokataIDE.register({id, commands, panels, keybindings}) there (see static/registry.js).

focus_row.description: the focused session's row (P33), or null

query.mokata: 1 = include the files mokata setup wrote (hidden by default, G23)

query.head: git ref or empty for the working tree

query.dir: optional: the directory whose children to list, repo-relative ('' = the root)
query.filter: optional: a case-insensitive substring matched against EVERY path (basename hits first); when set, `dir` is ignored
query.offset: optional: the page to start at — the previous answer's `next`
query.sync_ms: optional: how long (0..2000 ms) to wait for the answer before the 202 job handle (default 300)

query.outline: optional: 1 = include the file's outline (`outline`, the /api/outline answer) in the same response

query.sync_ms: optional: how long (0..2000 ms) to wait for the answer before the 202 job handle (default 300)
optional: how long (0..2000 ms) to wait for the answer before the 202 job handle (default 300)
optional: how long (0..2000 ms) to wait for the finished checks (default 300); past it the answer is still 200 — the CHECKING shape, with the job in `pending`
query.job: optional: the `pending` job id a page waited for — answers its finished rows

body.sync_ms: optional: how long (0..2000 ms) to wait before the 202 job handle (default 300)
body.offset: optional: the previous page's next_offset (default 0) — 0.0.26 P36 paging

body.sync_ms: optional: how long (0..2000 ms) to wait before the 202 job handle (default 300)

query.sync_ms: optional: how long (0..2000 ms) to wait for the answer before the 202 job handle (default 300)
query.page: optional: which page of PAGE_NODES nodes (1..; default 1) — a later page resumes the walk (P37: no hard cap)

body.*: a neutral event or a Claude Code hook payload

body.session: session id or null to leave
